messages.author: eb09e8497b635c23
messages.subject: odds or odds ratios
parts:
hello everybody,

I was wondering if somebody here is familiar with Peter Dalgaard's
Intro to Stats with R (2nd ed. 2008). I think there might be a teeny
tiny mistake in his discussion of logistic regression anlyses. my
little problem with the text is this:

On page 239 Peter briefly discusses the presentation of the results of
a logistic regression analysis in terms of odds ratio estimates (,
which I believe is quite common in linguistic publications).

he obtains the (alleged) odds ratios via

>exp (cbind (OR=coef(some.model), confint(that.model) ) ) # with confidence intervals

now, as R outputs these coefficients as logits, applying the
exponential function should give us odds (and not odds ratios).

however, Peter writes on that page:
"The (intercept) is really the odds of [some factor] and not an odds
ratio" suggesting that the remaining expressions labelled as "OR" here
are in fact odds ratios.

Long story short: OR should be a vector containing odds and not odds
ratios, right?

best,
daniel

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] odds or odds ratios
parts:
I don't have the second edition but it seems to me that he does get
odds ratios: The code below shows for the simplest possible logistic
regression that his line recreates 0.7218045.

# create some data
set.seed(11)
y <- factor(sample(letters[1:2], 100, replace=TRUE))
x <- factor(sample(letters[14:15], 100, replace=TRUE))

# compute odds ratio manually
table(x, y)
(30/19)/(35/16) # 0.7218045

# compute logistic regression on the data
model <- glm(y ~ x, family=binomial); summary(model)

# compute odds ratio w/ Dalgaard (2008)
exp(cbind(OR=coef(model), confint(model))) # 0.7218045 + CI

Cheers,
STG

>exp(coefficients)

regression coefficients are given as logits (log odds); so, if we apply exp( ) to coef, we should get odds

so, then my question would have to be:
if exp(coef) gives us in fact OR 8and not odds), why?

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] odds or odds ratios
parts:
> regression coefficients are given as logits (log odds); so, if we apply exp() to coef, we should get odds
Well, the regression coefficients indicate how much something
*changes*. Gelman and Hill (p. 82) should make this clear:
"Exponentiated logistic regression coefficients can be interpreted as
odds ratios." I don't really care that much about odds and odds ratios
anyway. I personally find them counterintuitive to interpret - no one
thinks in odds and odds ratios - and prefer to represent things in
(changes of) predicted probabilties (also nicely explained in Gelman
and Hill).

STG
